title: Connection Study Report (python-docx)
description: Upload a results.json (project metadata, bus voltages, fault results, conclusions) and get a fully-formatted Word .docx with cover page, executive summary, voltage profile + fault-level tables, and conclusions section. Saves about an hour per study and prevents copy-paste errors.

inputs.name: results.json
inputs.description: Project, executive_summary, network_description, assumptions[], bus_results[], fault_results[], conclusions[].

outputs.name: connection-study.docx
outputs.description: Word document — open in Word and press F9 to refresh fields if you add a TOC.

script:
import json
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH

with open('/input/results.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

doc = Document()
style = doc.styles['Normal']
style.font.name = 'Calibri'
style.font.size = Pt(11)

title = doc.add_paragraph()
title.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
run = title.add_run(data.get('project', 'Project'))
run.bold = True
run.font.size = Pt(28)
run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x29, 0x37)

subtitle = doc.add_paragraph()
subtitle.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
subtitle.add_run(f"Connection Study \u2014 {data.get('report_type', 'Load-flow & fault')}\n\n")
subtitle.add_run(f"Client: {data.get('client', '')}\n")
subtitle.add_run(f"Project ref: {data.get('project_ref', '')}\n")
subtitle.add_run(f"Date: {data.get('date', '')}")

doc.add_page_break()

doc.add_heading('1.  Executive Summary', level=1)
doc.add_paragraph(data.get('executive_summary', ''))

doc.add_heading('2.  Network and Modelling Assumptions', level=1)
doc.add_paragraph(data.get('network_description', ''))
doc.add_heading('Key assumptions', level=2)
for a in data.get('assumptions', []):
    doc.add_paragraph(a, style='List Bullet')

doc.add_heading('3.  Load-Flow Results', level=1)
tbl = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=4)
tbl.style = 'Light Grid Accent 1'
hdr = tbl.rows[0].cells
hdr[0].text = 'Bus'
hdr[1].text = 'Voltage (pu)'
hdr[2].text = 'Voltage (kV)'
hdr[3].text = 'Status'
for bus in data.get('bus_results', []):
    row = tbl.add_row().cells
    row[0].text = str(bus.get('name', ''))
    row[1].text = f"{bus.get('Vmag_pu', 0):.4f}"
    row[2].text = f"{bus.get('Vmag_kV', 0):.2f}"
    row[3].text = str(bus.get('status', ''))

doc.add_heading('4.  Fault Level Summary', level=1)
tbl = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=3)
tbl.style = 'Light Grid Accent 1'
hdr = tbl.rows[0].cells
hdr[0].text = 'Bus'
hdr[1].text = 'I_fault max (kA)'
hdr[2].text = 'Margin to breaker (%)'
for f in data.get('fault_results', []):
    row = tbl.add_row().cells
    row[0].text = str(f.get('bus', ''))
    row[1].text = f"{f.get('Imax_kA', 0):.2f}"
    row[2].text = f"{f.get('margin_pct', 0):.1f}%"

doc.add_heading('5.  Conclusions and Recommendations', level=1)
for c in data.get('conclusions', []):
    doc.add_paragraph(c, style='List Bullet')

doc.save('/output/connection-study.docx')
print('Wrote connection-study.docx')

If you keep a results.json as the single source of truth (solver writes it, this tool reads it), every report is byte-identical for unchanged data — no transcription errors.
